interest: This document is interesting for illustrating the far-reaching scope of wartime intelligence and psychological warfare during World War II, highlighting how diplomatic listening posts as far removed as Kabul monitored the regional impact of Japanese propaganda across South and Southeast Asia. For archival researchers and historians of diplomatic administration, it also offers a concise snapshot of the State Department's decimal indexing and cross-referencing practices, showing how despatches touching on multiple theaters and subjects (such as military activities, propaganda, and bilateral perceptions) were tracked across different decimal classifications.
overview: This file comprises a single Department of State 'List of Papers' cover sheet (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing documents filed under decimal file 894.20245C regarding Japanese military activities in Burma, including information gathering, espionage, and propaganda. The sheet records Despatch No. 263 dated August 19, 1943, sent from Afghanistan by U.S. diplomat Charles W. Thayer, which transmitted intelligence concerning the Afghan reaction to Japanese wartime propaganda in India and Burma. The sheet tracks distribution among State Department divisions and notes cross-references to related decimal files 894.20290h and 894.20245.

subfiles.summary: This State Department List of Papers (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, registers documentation under decimal file 894.20245C regarding Japanese military activities in Burma. It indexes Despatch No. 263 of August 19, 1943, authored by U.S. diplomat Charles W. Thayer in Afghanistan, which transmitted information on Afghan reactions to Japanese propaganda in India and Burma. The form records internal distribution to various departmental divisions (FC, DCR/1, NS, FE, PA/1, PS) and cross-references to files 894.20290h and 894.20245.
